# Headless Skills and Revocable UI Takeover Implementation Roadmap

- Status: `executing`
- Updated: `2026-11-13T16:03:43Z`

## Objective

Let authorized chat clients use the same application services as the UI, with optional exact-window takeover that the user can accept and immediately revoke while independent backend work continues; deliver desktop first, then server/browser support.

## Discovery

Read the entire supplied 1.0 design (18 invariants and 41 acceptance scenarios). Its reviewed commit 3f35f581 is historical. Initial discovery used b873a49f; publication was reconciled on rebuild at 3272dc4d54a0247aa9bf8544330a60efb83bb70e, source37dba8a596abcffe5191f70b7d4a7141f18c242cdf740022780b7c2d67a0923b, with unrelated dirty work preserved. The intervening checkpoint changes four support/guidance documents, not the inspected product seams. Shared System Builder use cases, revision-safe persistence and API/IPC parity exist. Desktop builds these providers inside registerDesktopIpc; Composer drafts remain separate from selectedSystem.revision, which is used as the save expectation. No general durable committed-change feed, universal operation receipt store, external builder MCP adapter or takeover authority was found in inspected owning seams. Existing runtime-workflow contracts are useful headlessly, but their advanced UI is not currently a Systems tab. This preparation changes no product code and asserts no executed product qualification.

### Security impact

- Disposition: `security-relevant`
- Summary: New external agent transport, delegated builder mutations, live UI-context flow, revocable exact-window authority, durable receipts/outbox replay and multi-worker delivery cross identity, isolation, persistence and privacy boundaries.
- Protected assets:
  - Principal/organization/workspace authority
  - Saved systems and immutable revision history
  - Human drafts and local navigation/focus
  - Live window context and protected content
  - Operation receipts, task handles and change-feed cursors
  - Credentials and bounded audit evidence
- Trust boundaries:
  - Chat/MCP process to authenticated desktop connector or managed API
  - Interactive exact owned UI session to takeover authority
  - Host command dispatch to local presentation gate/context publisher
  - Application transaction to receipt/outbox and authorized replay
  - Managed request scope to PostgreSQL RLS and subscriber workers
- Abuse and failure cases:
  - Agent self-grants takeover or inherits renderer/admin rights
  - Spoofed host/window/workspace or stale request/readiness/revoke changes newer authority
  - Delayed command or context producer applies/publishes after revoke
  - Refresh silently overwrites dirty draft or launders its revision expectation
  - Retry duplicates a mutation or discloses revoked/cross-tenant receipt
  - Lost/gapped event delivery steers detached navigation or regresses state
  - Unbounded requests/queues/replay exhaust resources
  - Resource text injects instructions or diagnostics leak secrets/private drafts
- Controls:
  - Host-derived stable principal/organization and finite delegated scopes; interactive acceptance credentials separate from agent credentials
  - Exact host/UI/agent/request/attempt/lease/generation binding with one reserved controller and terminal ended authority
  - Synchronous local fence and per-command generation before every effect; context checks before collection and publication
  - Immutable draft base and explicit save-or-cancel handoff
  - Transactional bounded receipt/outbox, stable retry identity and current reauthorization
  - Scoped at-least-once feed, snapshot/cursor contract and guarded refetch
  - Finite schemas/time/size/rate/retention bounds; metadata-only context; structured redacted audit
  - Disable entry points and revoke grants for rollback; retain protected data/receipts and never restore insecure fallback
- Verification:
  - Deterministic fake-clock transition/race/queue tests
  - Transport denial, malformed/oversized, origin/host and exact-frame tests
  - SQLite/PostgreSQL atomicity, replay, retry and cross-tenant tests
  - Rendered draft/context/focus/fencing interaction tests
  - Real packaged Windows Electron and local Chrome journeys with automated accept/revoke and owned shutdown
  - Exact-source executed receipts and separate-invocation review; actual managed qualification remains distinct
- Residual risks:
  - Compromised OS account/main process or managed administrator can cross local boundaries
  - Already transmitted context cannot be recalled
  - Backend jobs keep only their existing recovery/cancellation guarantees; host exit is outside continuity scope
  - Browser background throttling and target ingress/IdP/database behavior need actual qualification
  - No public-internet abuse hardening, new identity provider or relay is approved

### Constraints

- User approved desktop-first then server/browser strategy only; roadmap approval and implementation authority are not granted.
- Before publication, reconcile the new root-provided source baseline and preserve unrelated dirty files, legacy roadmaps and current qualification. Planning is ignored-only until explicit root publication handoff.
- Use one desktop host and one authoritative service/persistence set. MCP stdio adapter forwards to authenticated loopback desktop connector or existing authenticated server API. No second backend/database and no new OAuth issuer.
- Initial connector delegation and presentation/context authority require a successor ADR/threat-control update before implementation. Ordinary agent grants exclude credentials, admin, release/deploy/publish, arbitrary execution and policy mutation.
- Server/browser parity targets the same server deployment used by that browser. Desktop-server synchronization, cloud-to-local relay, background work after desktop host exit, general desktop control, independent branches and collaborative editing remain excluded.
- All technical acceptance is executable by agents. Product acceptance/revoke buttons remain explicit human controls; automated UI tests perform the clicks. No participant studies, owner-review acceptance tasks or invented passes.
- Use focused checks for chunks and relevant completion checks per increment; reserve one test:all and applicable repository-wide final gates for after all implementation chunks. Preparation runs no apps, models, dependency installs or full suites.
- Current deployments stay single replica; multi-worker claims require a two-worker controlled fixture and later real target qualification. No production mutation, scaling, remote publication or supplied credential access is authorized by this roadmap.

## High-level decisions

### Choose the host rollout

Which host rollout should the roadmap cover?

The design spans a running desktop instance and a managed server/browser deployment. They share application semantics but have different authentication, lifecycle, delivery and qualification boundaries.

- Status: `approved`
- Selected option: `desktop-then-server-browser`

| Option | Summary | Recommended | Tradeoffs | Consequences |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Desktop first, then server/browser (desktop-then-server-browser) | Deliver one existing desktop host first, then the same capabilities through the existing authenticated server and browser. | yes | Covers both requested interfaces with controlled sequencing; Requires actual packaged desktop, browser and managed persistence evidence | Use typed stdio MCP forwarding to the desktop connector or existing server API; Defer cloud-to-local relay and work after desktop host exit; No desktop-server synchronization or new OAuth issuer |
| Server/browser first, then desktop (server-browser-then-desktop) | Qualify the existing managed server and browser first, then add the running desktop connector. | no | Begins with established managed identity; Delays the existing-desktop experience and front-loads managed qualification | Same final two-host scope in a different order; Desktop provider extraction occurs later |
| Desktop only (desktop-only) | Deliver the bounded desktop workflow and defer server/browser support to a successor roadmap. | no | Smallest first scope; Does not cover the design's hosted interface in this roadmap | Managed parity and cross-worker delivery remain explicitly pending successor work |

## Increment 1: Use chat tools to author systems and keep saved data synchronized

- Id: `headless-authoring-and-synchronization`
- Status: `implementing`
- Dependencies: None

Deliver an independently useful headless builder workflow through the existing desktop host, with revision-safe semantic edits, durable retries, normal UI refresh and protected human drafts before adding window control.

### Work packages

- **Connect to the running host** (`shared-host-connector`): Extract narrow lazy providers used by IPC and an authenticated loopback connector; a typed stdio MCP adapter discovers the same host and finite delegated capabilities.
- **Author through shared services** (`semantic-tools-and-receipts`): Workspace/template/system discovery, create/rename/clone, preview/apply semantic batches, supported workflow preparation/invocation and task status use application authorization, immutable revisions and durable scoped receipts.
- **Refresh saved data safely** (`committed-changes-and-drafts`): Transactional outbox and scoped cursor/read delivery update normal UI data without steering navigation; immutable draft bases and guarded refetch/save preserve human work.
- **Package and prove useful headless work** (`portable-skill-and-host-proof`): Portable control skill, generated finite tool reference, focused tests and a real packaged desktop external-tool journey prove supported behavior without any takeover lease.

### Deliverables

- Successor ADR for desktop connector/delegation and shared authority, plus updates to decision readiness, host model, System Builder, persistence, security threat/control guidance and relevant README/context sources.
- Narrow host provider seam, authenticated loopback connector, versioned contract families and runtime validation, official SDK-backed stdio MCP adapter with an evidenced client/SDK protocol matrix.
- Shared application semantic edit preview/apply for add/configure/connect/move-or-reparent/remove with validated consequences; existing full-revision save remains the authoritative persistence path.
- Durable organization/principal/registered-client/workspace/operation receipts and transactional committed-change outbox; scoped snapshot/cursor, deduplication, replay and resynchronization contract.
- Immutable Composer draft-base record/revision identity, conflict-aware clean/dirty/saving/archive refresh and late-result fencing; externally started task discovery reusing current observation patterns.
- Portable skills/control-ai-system-builder package, routing/installation guidance and behavior tests; actual isolated packaged desktop qualification definition and bounded sanitized observation schema.

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |

Starting the MCP adapter must not start a second application host, open its own desktop database or start a model on a passive read. Only the finite typed tool catalog is exposed. Incompatible versions, unknown tools/fields and unsupported execution, cancellation or streaming must fail clearly. No arbitrary HTTP executor, code, selector or shell capability is permitted. | local | not recorded |
| `revision-safe-semantic-authoring`: Tools must resolve explicit workspace, system, template and exact asset IDs before mutation, then support available template creation, rename, clone and bounded preview/apply composition edits. Semantic batches must validate add, allowed configuration, compatible connections, placement changes and removal consequences in the application. Preview has no side effect; applying one valid batch creates one immutable revision against the supplied original base. The same application validation and authorization must apply to UI and agent calls. Stale bases, wrong ownership, incompatible ports, protected nodes, invalid configuration and malformed or oversized batches must fail without a partial mutation. | local | not recorded |
| `durable-retries-and-current-authority`: Supported retriable mutations must store a durable receipt under verified organization, stable principal, registered client, workspace, operation kind and idempotency key, with a canonical input fingerprint and result or task handle. A reconnect or new chat session must keep that receipt identity. Equal input returns the original result or in-progress handle; different input under the same key is rejected. Uncertain external effects must reconcile an operation record before another side effect. The current caller must be authorized before any saved receipt or result is returned, including after membership revocation. Guessed keys and cross-tenant/client/workspace requests must disclose no result. For supported transactional mutations, business writes, receipt and outbox commit or roll back together. Advertise bounded retention and an explicit expired-key reconciliation response; never claim universal exactly-once effects or retry an expired unknown operation automatically. | local | not recorded |
| `committed-change-delivery`: IPC, API, agent and supported background mutations must publish scoped committed resource metadata through one application/persistence seam. A rollback emits no committed event, and events must omit drafts, prompts, credentials and arbitrary instructions. A transactionally persisted outbox must recover after a commit followed by dispatcher failure. At-least-once consumers deduplicate IDs and older revisions, and snapshot/cursor setup must close the initial read/subscription race. Valid scoped cursors replay retained events; gaps, expired retention and invalid cursors require a scoped authoritative resynchronization. Subscriptions, replay and refetch recheck current read authorization. Normal data events may refresh lists and task status but must not open resources, change navigation, move focus or select previews as an indirect automation path. | local | not recorded |
| `draft-base-and-refetch-ownership`: A loaded draft must retain immutable base record revision and revision ID until an explicit successful save, reload or rebase. New list metadata must never advance that base. Clean editors may install current saved state while preserving compatible selection. Dirty editors retain draft and undo history and show a newer saved revision; archived or unavailable resources retain recoverable work. A stale save must conflict without overwriting either writer. Saving and refetch results must match the captured workspace, resource, subscription and request generation. Reverse-order replies cannot regress the displayed saved revision, cross a workspace switch, overwrite a dirty draft or update a newer operation. | local | not recorded |

Status polling must be scoped and non-starting, and cancellation is exposed only where the operation really implements it. Document actual synchronous, recovery and host-lifetime limits. The skill must keep backend operation and presentation outcomes separate and must not repeat a successful mutation just to reveal it. The skill and generated tool reference must contain no credentials and grant no authority. Untrusted resource text or tool output cannot extend tool scope, request secrets or authorize publication, execution or policy changes. | local | not recorded |

The real UI must reflect external rename and saved composition changes without manual reload, preserve a dirty draft and original base during a competing save, and return a stale-write conflict. A visible toast or canned response alone cannot pass. ### Verification

- Extend System Builder use-case/repository/API-IPC parity and Composer tests; add fixed-router connector/MCP, semantic, receipt/outbox and denial cases.
- Run real SQLite/Electron commit/rollback, lost-response, dispatch-failure and restart tests; run packaged-desktop-headless-authoring.e2e.spec.ts in the one-worker harness with credential capture off and owned cleanup.
- Run relevant docs/architecture/agent-support, desktop type/build/package and conditional dependency-security gates. Defer aggregates.

### Rollback

Disable connector discovery/admission, revoke its delegated client credentials and stop its listeners/adapter processes; restore existing IPC-only composition without opening a second database. Retain immutable revisions, business receipts and outbox/audit records under their access policy. Stop dispatch safely and resynchronize ordinary UI from saved records. Apply only compatible additive-schema rollback; never delete newer data or restore unauthenticated/permissive access.

### Excluded

- UI takeover and live window context until increment2
- New execution engines, provider/model downloads, general shell/HTTP tools, renderer-form automation, hidden drafts and automatic release/deployment
- Server/browser parity until increment3; desktop-server synchronization, cloud-to-local relay and post-host-exit work throughout

## Increment 2: Accept and revoke automation control of one desktop window

- Id: `revocable-desktop-presentation`
- Status: `pending`
- Dependencies: `headless-authoring-and-synchronization`

Let a user explicitly attach an agent to one desktop window and revoke it immediately, while headless authority, saved-data synchronization and independent tasks continue.

### Work packages

- **Reserve and activate exact authority** (`exact-window-authority`): Host/UI/agent incarnations, bounded requests, acceptance attempts, terminal leases and readiness transitions enforce one controller per window with distinct interactive authority.
- **Control the window and preserve human work** (`shell-gate-and-handoff`): Persistent accept/decline/activate/revoke shell controls, save-or-cancel dirty-draft handoff and a local fence restore human control before network work.
- **Fence every presentation and observation** (`presentation-context-and-delivery`): Finite semantic actions and minimal context use exact lease and command generations, ordered bounded delivery, separate acknowledgments and revocation-aware asynchronous guards.
- **Prove revocation and continuity** (`race-lifecycle-and-host-journeys`): Deterministic scheduler tests and real packaged desktop scenarios exercise delayed grants, readiness, revokes, commands, callbacks, context, reconnect and independent backend work.

### Deliverables

- Successor ADR and current architecture/threat-model guidance defining UI authority independent of backend grants, exact targeting, terminal revocation, delivery queues, minimal context, draft handoff and lifecycle recovery.
- Framework-neutral UI-control contracts/ports/application state machine, finite IPC/preload surfaces, bounded host authority/delivery stores and exact owned-window registration.
- Shared takeover provider, persistent app-shell controls, local presentation gate/context publisher and first allowlisted desktop actions with complete async fencing.
- Typed request/lease/attempt/generation lifecycle and presentation acknowledgments; skill request/status/reveal/release behavior that continues headlessly after detachment.
- Source-linked INV/AT coverage, deterministic race and privacy tests, automated accessibility/focus checks, actual packaged desktop journeys and measured revocation/delivery targets.

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exact-window-acceptance-and-reservation`: Only an authenticated interactive UI session from the exact live owned window main frame may accept or signal readiness for its displayed current request. Ordinary agent credentials must be unable to invoke these operations. A grant must bind host incarnation, UI incarnation, stable agent session, verified principal/organization, workspace, request, acceptance attempt, lease generation, allowed actions/context and expiry. A lease ID by itself is not authorization. Grant creation must atomically reserve one window through awaiting-readiness and active states. A second agent cannot displace an active or activating reservation. Readiness must match the current unexpired, unrevoked reservation and local attempt/fence before either gate becomes active. Pending, declined, expired, failed and not-ready requests provide no presentation or fresh UI context. Workspace changes end the scope or require a fresh explicitly accepted request. | local | not recorded |
| `dirty-handoff-and-reachable-controls`: The app shell must show the identified session, task, workspace and exact window request with Accept automation takeover and Decline controls. Activating and active states must retain a Revoke automation takeover control outside managed feature content. A clean draft may proceed. A dirty editor must offer Save changes and accept takeover or Cancel takeover, with no silent save, discard or unsupported preserved-draft claim. A save conflict, validation failure or transport failure keeps manual control and the complete draft. During takeover one controller owns navigation and editing in the managed work area; competing human edits are disabled while reading/status and revoke stay usable. Revoke needs no confirmation and remains keyboard reachable across loading, ordinary dialogs, feature navigation and backend failure. After revoke, restore human controls in place without reverting saved changes, replacing the route or discarding work, and state that independent chat work may continue. Automated tests must verify focus, native control semantics, keyboard reachability and bounded narrow layouts. | local | not recorded |
| `immediate-local-revocation-and-exact-retry`: When the revoke handler runs, capture the exact immutable request/attempt/lease target, mark control inactive, increment the local fence, clear the presentation gate, discard queues and unsent context, invalidate producers, abort presentation-only work where supported and restore human controls before any awaited transport call. Host revoke must be idempotent and serialize against acceptance for the same attempt, including cancellation before the UI knows a lease ID. Reject partial or contradictory targets; never broaden cancellation or substitute a later current lease during retries. Late grants, old acceptance retries, delayed readiness, heartbeat/reconnect and queued messages must never recreate ended authority. Sufficient terminal request/lease state and unknown-ID refusal must preserve this property within the advertised retry/retention policy. An old revoke for lease A must not end later accepted lease B. Network loss may leave host acknowledgment pending but local human control remains immediate; reconnect retries only the captured target. New control needs a fresh accepted request. | local | not recorded |
| `presentation-effect-fencing`: Initial presentation is a finite validated action family: open system, select component, show run, show artifact and show validation results using explicit authorized resource IDs. No DOM selector, route executor, JavaScript or business mutation is permitted in a presentation handler. Before starting and immediately before every visible side effect, each handler must verify exact host/UI/workspace/lease/generation, local fence and command execution generation plus cancellation, expiry and preconditions. No asynchronous gap may follow the final effect guard. Held reads, preview preparation, navigation completions, timers, animation callbacks and late result handlers from ended or superseded commands must remain inert even if an abort fails. A removed resource returns a bounded failure without replacement navigation. Events, default-selection effects and successful backend callbacks must not become indirect focus/navigation paths outside the gate, including after revoke or a workspace change. | local | not recorded |
| `serial-delivery-and-independent-deduplication`: Use a bounded serial per-lease queue with host-assigned increasing sequences and finite command ID/payload receipts. The same ID/payload returns its recorded status without a repeated effect; changed payload under the same ID is rejected. Completed lower sequences do not reapply. A bounded higher-sequence gap requests missing positions from the host buffer; it must not silently skip actions. Unrecoverable gaps end attachment and return human control while backend work continues. A timeout or expired command records a terminal result, invalidates its own execution generation and only then advances the queue. A callback from that command cannot override later presentation under the same still-active lease. No implicit last-request-wins coalescing or replay into a newer lease is allowed. Acknowledgments must distinguish host acceptance, delivery, applied/already-applied, rejected and discarded; business idempotency never substitutes for presentation ordering. | local | not recorded |
| `context-minimization-and-revoke-fence`: Accepted context initially contains only permitted workspace/resource IDs, supported view, attached-window readiness and dirty-navigation blocking. Unsaved text, form contents, screenshots, secrets and protected prompts are not implicitly shared. Context producers must check current lease/scope/fence before collection and again before publication. Local revoke prevents new work, discards unsent values and suppresses held async results; host revoke stops forwarding and discards its queued values. Fresh context requests after revoke must be denied even when the client ignores notifications. Bytes already transmitted may still arrive and cannot be recalled; this limit must be clear without treating independent authorized backend reads as window observation. The skill must receive or poll truthful attachment status, stop trying presentation after detach and avoid repeated takeover requests after explicit revoke unless the user asks to attach again. | local | not recorded |
| `backend-continuity-and-lifecycle-isolation`: A backend save finishing after revoke and another permitted backend command afterward must succeed under current backend authority; ordinary UI data/task updates continue without forced focus, selection or navigation. A supported long-running backend operation must retain its existing task lifecycle and remain inspectable by chat and UI after revoke. UI revocation must not call task cancellation or close the chat connection. Agent targets stay explicit when the human selects another workspace. Reload/new window incarnation, host restart, lease expiry, voluntary release and control-connection loss must return or default to human control without old-lease replay. Heartbeats can renew only the same current active grant, never ended authority. Different windows may hold independent leases; revoking one leaves the other unchanged. Logout or backend access loss applies the existing broader access policy and ends attachment; continuation after UI revoke never permits unauthorized backend work. A successful backend mutation with detached or failed reveal must report two outcomes and never retry the mutation to obtain a UI success. Host-exit task durability and physical cancellation remain outside this guarantee. | local | not recorded |
| `desktop-takeover-real-host`: An automated isolated packaged Windows journey must use a real MCP client and live host connector to request the identified window, click Accept automation takeover, reveal a newly created saved system and start an existing supported observable backend operation. The test must hold a presentation response/context producer, click Revoke automation takeover, navigate and edit as the user, finish the backend operation and another scoped save, then verify ordinary data refresh without old preview/focus/navigation or fresh context. ### Verification

- Use fake clocks and held promises for AT09/10/11/12/13/14/26/27/38/39/41: grant/cancel/ready/revoke permutations and same-lease timeout races.

### Rollback

Disable new takeover requests, synchronously close all local presentation/context gates and restore manual controls, then exactly terminate pending/active reservations and stop delivery. Preserve headless connector authorization and independent tasks from increment1, ordinary data subscriptions, immutable revisions and drafts. Retain terminal authority records for stale retry refusal; never reuse generations or reenable a prior lease after rollback.

### Excluded

- General desktop/window-manager control, arbitrary route/DOM/JavaScript execution and direct renderer form editing
- Preserve-draft acceptance until an actual complete recovery store exists; shared-window collaborative editing and per-agent data branches
- Continuity after host exit, new task durability/cancellation guarantees and server/browser support before increment3

## Increment 3: Deliver the same workflow through the authenticated server and browser

- Id: `server-browser-and-delivery-qualification`
- Status: `pending`
- Dependencies: `revocable-desktop-presentation`

Qualify shared headless/control behavior on the existing managed server and browser, with PostgreSQL durability, authenticated streaming/replay and evidenced multi-worker delivery, without introducing desktop-server synchronization or a relay.

### Work packages

- **Use the existing managed authority** (`managed-api-and-browser`): Stdio MCP forwarding and finite API routes use existing bearer/OIDC membership and application policy; shared browser takeover and synchronization clients preserve identical semantics.
- **Recover and deliver committed state** (`postgres-replay-and-workers`): PostgreSQL receipt/outbox coordination and authenticated header-capable stream/polling clients recover across reconnect and dispatch failure; bounded two-worker fixtures prove subscriber reach without an external broker.
- **Prove both real interfaces** (`parity-and-final-evidence`): Automated local Chrome and packaged Windows journeys, full INV/AT mapping, measured targets and final candidate-bound gates support truthful deployment capability declarations.

### Deliverables

- Server/browser ADR and host/API/identity/persistence/threat-model updates for the same-server topology, interactive UI credential separation, authenticated streaming, outbox ownership and worker coordination; deployment defaults remain single replica.
- Finite explicit API route-policy entries, principal-aware managed connector/tool forwarding, shared browser shell/gate/context integration and scoped authenticated stream with bounded polling fallback.
- PostgreSQL transactional receipts/outbox, bounded worker claim/recovery/delivery adapter and cursor retention/resync behavior with organization RLS and current authorization.
- Agent-executable local Chrome/server/PostgreSQL and packaged Windows acceptance definitions, source-coverage crosswalk, bounded evidence schemas, operator configuration/rollback guide and capability/qualification matrix.
- Current exact-target receipts and separate-invocation reviews for increment criteria, then one final all-suite and repository-wide completion run after every implementation chunk is complete; no implied production/public release.

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `same-server-authority-and-route-parity`: The browser and agent adapter must identify and use the same server deployment and application providers. Each agent request uses existing supported bearer/OIDC identity, explicit organization selection, active membership and application workspace authorization. New finite API/stream routes must be registered in the existing deny-by-default policy with matching operation envelopes and runtime validation. Interactive acceptance/readiness/revoke credentials must remain distinct from ordinary agent grants. Server, IPC and MCP mappings must preserve the same semantic authoring, expected revisions, task/approval denials and separate operation/presentation outcomes. No new OAuth issuer, identity system, external relay, direct desktop database connection or desktop-server synchronization is introduced. | local | not recorded |
| `authenticated-browser-stream-and-refresh`: Use an authenticated header-capable HTTP stream for application changes and separate logical presentation/context channels, with bounded scoped polling/resynchronization when streaming is unavailable. Never put long-lived credentials in stream URLs. Snapshot/cursor setup, replay, resource refetch and permission changes must preserve organization/workspace isolation, immutable dirty-draft bases, monotonic saved state and subscription/request generation guards. Duplicate events, replay gaps, expired cursors, reverse-order reads, abandoned subscriptions and background-tab resume must converge to authorized current saved state without implicit reveal/focus/navigation after detach. | local | not recorded |
| `postgres-atomicity-and-worker-delivery`: PostgreSQL business mutation, receipt and outbox must commit consistently under current organization scope and row security; failed or retried serializable callbacks must not duplicate side effects. A controlled fixture with two real server workers sharing the same test PostgreSQL must deliver committed notifications to subscribers connected to either worker. Kill dispatch after commit, restart it and prove retained replay or scoped resync without a lost committed result. Worker claim/retry/expiry and retention must be finite and fail closed. Duplicate dispatch is allowed only under at-least-once semantics with idempotent consumers; no universal exactly-once, external-effect recovery or model-job durability is claimed. A two-worker fixture does not authorize deployment scaling. Existing single-replica templates stay unchanged until the target ingress, identity provider, RLS runtime role, database and worker topology have actual qualification. | controlled-environment | not recorded |
| `browser-real-host-and-parity`: An automated local Chrome journey must use the built thin client, a real authenticated test server and PostgreSQL, and an actual stdio MCP client forwarding to that same server. Use synthetic accounts and isolated organization/workspaces without production credentials. Discover a supported template, create and edit its saved system headlessly, click Accept automation takeover in the target tab, reveal saved work, start an existing observable operation, click Revoke automation takeover and continue backend work while the human navigates/edits elsewhere. Prove dirty-base conflict, no stale preview/focus/navigation, no fresh context after revoke, lost-response retry, reverse refetch, readiness/grant/revoke races, multi-tab isolation, expiration, disconnect and fresh acceptance after reload. Drive product human buttons automatically. Reexecute the focused packaged desktop journey on the same final candidate to establish retained desktop behavior. Complete the 18-invariant/41-scenario crosswalk with exact test and host owners; deterministic substitutes must state their limits and cannot stand in for real host, persistence or native evidence. | controlled-environment | not recorded |
| `host-specific-targets-and-bounds`: Record Windows/Electron and Chrome/server/PostgreSQL versions, machine resources, foreground/background status, network fixture and sample counts. Collect a baseline and report actual p50/p95/max separately for each host; no draft number is a measured claim. For 100 bounded local Chrome mutations after warm-up, commit-to-current-visible-state p95 must be at most 2000 ms and warm allowed presentation p95 at most 1000 ms. For 100 local revokes, restored human controls must meet p95 at most 100 ms and maximum 250 ms after the handler begins, independent of server acknowledgment. Healthy local reconnect/replay/resync must yield authorized current state within 5000 ms. Retest background-throttled expiry/liveness and both UI command/context size and queue bounds; zero old-generation effects and zero newly published revoked context are absolute correctness requirements. Measure queue depth, duplicate suppression, conflicts, retry receipts and sanitized audit counters. Failed targets remain failed or pending and require explicit policy revision; local timing does not qualify WAN or cloud latency. | controlled-environment | not recorded |

Existing OIDC, membership, RLS and secret boundaries remain authoritative. Automated denial/failure tests must cover absent/revoked/wrong-audience credentials, wrong role or organization/workspace/window, agent self-acceptance, changed membership before replay/receipt reads, unknown/noncanonical route variants, malformed/oversized traffic and policy/stream/database failures. Verify current access before returning replayed events, receipts or refetched resources. Failed authorization ends attachment and prevents new backend operations under existing policy, unlike ordinary UI-only revoke. Credential-bearing traces, screenshots and raw logs must not be retained; tests use bounded synthetic evidence. Rollback disables the new routes/stream/control surface and ends leases while retaining existing secure APIs, data/receipts/audit, drafts and normal authorized UI access. | local | not recorded |

No race, draft, privacy, retry, delivery, authority or business/presentation distinction may disappear when scenarios are grouped. After every implementation chunk in all three increments is recorded and relevant checks pass, run npm run test:all once, followed by applicable docs:check, architecture:check, agent-support:check, dependency security and server/thin-client/desktop build-package gates on the current candidate. ### Verification

- Run focused managed API/route-policy/workflow parity, organization/RLS, authenticated stream and PostgreSQL receipt/outbox denial/recovery tests.
- Run thin-client-headless-takeover.e2e.spec.ts with real Chrome/server/PostgreSQL/stdio MCP, two-worker dispatch-crash/replay/access-loss tests and the final packaged desktop journey. Disable credential capture; own cleanup.
- After all chunks, run the serial overall test:all and applicable repository gates/builds. Preserve unrelated work and separate target-environment evidence.

### Rollback

Disable new agent/control/change-stream route admission and revoke affected delegated credentials and leases; close browser gates locally and end exact host reservations. Stop outbox dispatch/worker claims safely without deleting committed records, receipts, terminal lease state or audit. Fall back to existing authorized UI/API reads and scoped resync, preserve RLS and draft bases, and roll back only compatible additive schema/application changes. Never restore insecure dev/no-auth modes, broad cancellation or implicit lease reacquisition.

### Excluded

- Cloud chat access to a local desktop, authenticated relay, remote desktop control, background daemon after desktop exit and desktop-server replication/synchronization
- New OAuth/OIDC issuer/login UX, public MCP hosting, external broker dependency, internet-wide hardening and production scaling/deployment without separate decisions and actual qualification
- Universal exactly-once external effects, new model/runtime recovery or cancellation promises, independent agent branches/merge, collaborative editing, screenshots/unsaved-text context and arbitrary renderer editing
